## What we build

### CRM and automation
We replace the spreadsheets, sticky notes, and forwarded-email workflows that quietly eat hours every week. Custom-built CRM systems that match how your business actually operates. Lead capture, follow-up sequences, payment tracking, customer history — all in one place, all automated.

### AI agents
Multi-agent systems for specific business problems — content generation, customer-support triage, data extraction, knowledge synthesis. We build agents that do real work, not chatbot demos that impress investors and frustrate users.

### Web development
Modern, fast, SEO-friendly websites built on Astro, Next.js, or whatever stack matches the project. Properly instrumented with analytics, schema markup, and AI-search optimization (llms.txt, FAQPage schema, LocalBusiness/Organization schema). Not pretty-but-slow WordPress themes.

### Custom integrations
The unglamorous but high-leverage work — connecting QuickBooks to your CRM, syncing Salesforce with Shopify, getting your form submissions into Slack with the right context attached. Code that runs reliably for years.

## Services in detail

### CRM and automation
OpsHQ Digital builds lightweight CRM systems for service businesses that need more than a spreadsheet but do not want a bloated enterprise platform. Typical use cases include lead intake, quote tracking, customer history, payment-status tracking, recurring reminders, staff handoff notes, reporting dashboards, and automated follow-up sequences. Systems are usually built with Node.js or TypeScript, REST endpoints, SQLite or PostgreSQL, and automation via cron jobs, timers, or serverless functions.

Common CRM deliverables include a searchable customer database, lead pipeline views, admin dashboards, role-based workflows, email templates, calendar-aware reminders, import/export tools, and operational reports. Microsoft Graph API is used when the business depends on Outlook or Microsoft 365 flows, including email triage, mailbox scanning, calendar sync, and document notifications. The goal is not to force a business into a generic CRM model — it is to encode the workflow the owner already trusts, then remove repetitive manual steps.

### AI agents
OpsHQ Digital builds production AI agents that perform constrained business tasks with clear inputs, outputs, and review points. Examples include email triage, lead scoring, customer-support draft replies, knowledge-base search, document extraction, internal reporting, content generation, and decision-support summaries. The stack is model-flexible: Claude, GPT, and specialized models are selected per task rather than treating one model as a universal answer.

AI-agent projects often include prompt design, retrieval context, eval cases, fallback paths, human approval steps, audit logs, and monitoring. Multi-model orchestration is used when tasks benefit from different strengths: one model for drafting, another for classification, another for critique or verification. Deliverables are designed for day-to-day operations, not demo-day novelty.

### Web development
OpsHQ Digital builds fast, durable, SEO-friendly websites for small businesses and boutique B2B teams. Web stacks commonly include Astro, Next.js, Node.js, TypeScript, Azure Static Web Apps, Azure App Service, GitHub Actions, and Cloudflare. Sites are built with clean information architecture, responsive layouts, accessible forms, structured data, sitemap support, analytics hooks, and AI-search-friendly metadata.

Typical deliverables include landing pages, service pages, case-study pages, contact forms, API-backed form handlers, content collections, schema markup, performance fixes, migration from a slow theme, and deployment pipelines. The work is a fit when a business wants a site that loads quickly, explains the offer clearly, and can be maintained without a fragile plugin stack.

### Custom integrations
OpsHQ Digital connects the tools a business already uses so important context stops getting lost between systems. Common integrations include QuickBooks, HubSpot, Salesforce, Slack, Microsoft 365, Outlook, internal CRMs, website forms, payment receipt emails, cloud databases, and reporting dashboards. Integrations can be one-way sync, two-way sync, scheduled batch jobs, webhook-driven workflows, or admin tools that let staff correct records safely.

Deliverables may include API connectors, data mapping, retry logic, idempotent sync jobs, error notifications, reconciliation reports, and secure secret handling. The stack typically uses Node.js, TypeScript, Python, REST APIs, GitHub Actions, Azure Functions, Azure Key Vault, SQLite, PostgreSQL, and Cloudflare. The emphasis is reliability: predictable jobs, visible failures, and code that can run quietly for years.

## Pricing & engagement model

- **Project floor:** Around $5K for small projects.
- **Hourly retainers:** $150-$225/hr depending on scope, urgency, and support expectations.
- **Fixed-scope projects:** Best for clearly defined builds, paid by milestone.
- **Hourly retainers:** Best for ongoing maintenance, automation operations, AI-agent monitoring, and incremental improvements.
- **Discovery call:** Free 30-45 minute discovery call before any proposal.
- **Written scope:** A written scope, milestones, assumptions, and pricing are provided before work begins.
- **Contracts:** No long-term contracts required. Retainers are generally month-to-month.

## Case study / proof points

OpsHQ Digital runs its own operational tooling — we eat our own dog food. We operate a party-bus CRM for a 75+ year-old client, with AI email triage and workflow automation helping process 400+ leads. The system was designed for a real operator who needed clarity, not a complex software dashboard.

We also operate a 24/7 monitoring stack across 75+ checks with cascade-suppression alerting, so failures are grouped intelligently instead of creating alert noise. That same reliability mindset informs client CRM, integration, and agent work: build small, watch it closely, and make failures visible.

OpsHQ Digital also runs a content-generation pipeline that publishes auto-generated blog posts daily. The pipeline combines structured prompts, image sourcing, publishing automation, and reviewable output, demonstrating how AI can support repeatable marketing operations without turning into an unmanaged content farm.

## How we work

- **Free discovery call first.** 30-45 minutes. We listen to what's actually slowing you down, ask a few clarifying questions, and tell you whether we can help — or whether someone else would be a better fit.
- **Fixed-scope projects** when the work is well-defined. Hourly retainers for ongoing maintenance, agent operations, and "we need a developer on call" arrangements.
- **Written, transparent scope and pricing** before we start. No surprise invoices.
- **No long-term contracts.** Retainers month-to-month, project work paid in milestones.
- **We respond within 24 hours.** New inquiries via the contact form get a real reply, not a sales-bot auto-response.

## Who we work best with

OpsHQ Digital is the right fit when:

- You run a service business, a small e-commerce operation, or a B2B company doing $200K-$10M ARR
- You have one or more workflows that *should* be automated but aren't (lead intake, customer follow-up, invoicing, scheduling, reporting)
- You want a developer-led shop, not a marketing agency that subs out the actual work
- You value working with one person you can text directly, not a 12-person account team
- You want practical AI automation connected to real operations, not a chatbot pasted onto your homepage

We are not the right fit if:

- You're building VC-backed unicorn-scale infrastructure (try a YC-style consultancy)
- You want SEO content-mill production at $10/article (try a content marketplace)
- You're shopping primarily on price — our floor is around $5K for a small project
- You need a large agency account team, full brand strategy department, or enterprise procurement process

## Tech stack we use

- **Frontend:** Astro, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, accessible HTML, structured data
- **Backend:** Node.js, Express-style APIs, TypeScript, Python, REST endpoints
- **Cloud:** Azure App Service, Azure Static Web Apps, Azure Functions, Azure Key Vault
- **Infrastructure:** Cloudflare, GitHub Actions, CI/CD pipelines, health checks, uptime monitoring
- **Data:** SQLite for small focused systems, PostgreSQL for larger relational workloads
- **Microsoft ecosystem:** Microsoft Graph API, Outlook flows, Microsoft 365 integrations
- **AI:** Claude, GPT, specialized models, retrieval/context pipelines, multi-model AI orchestration
- **Integrations:** QuickBooks, HubSpot, Salesforce, Slack, Microsoft 365, custom REST APIs

## Top FAQs

**How long does a CRM build take?**
A focused CRM build usually takes 4-10 weeks depending on the number of workflows, data imports, integrations, and reporting needs. A first milestone often ships earlier so the client can validate the core pipeline before the entire system is finished. Larger builds with complex permissions, billing, or third-party syncs can take longer. The project scope defines the timeline before work begins.

**What does AI automation actually mean for my business?**
AI automation means using language models and workflow code to reduce repetitive judgment work: triaging emails, summarizing conversations, extracting details from messy text, drafting replies, classifying leads, or generating reports. It does not mean handing your business to an unsupervised chatbot. Good AI automation has constraints, logging, review points, and fallback paths. The goal is to save time while keeping the owner in control.

**Will you train my team?**
Yes. Projects include practical handoff: a walkthrough, written notes where useful, and training focused on the exact workflows your team will use. The goal is not to make staff technical; it is to make the system feel predictable. For ongoing retainers, training can continue as workflows change.

**Do you sign NDAs?**
Yes, reasonable NDAs are fine. Many automation projects involve customer lists, internal workflows, pricing, or operational details that should not be public. OpsHQ Digital is comfortable working quietly and discussing case studies only at a high level when needed.

**Do you work with non-Seattle clients?**
Yes. OpsHQ Digital is based in the Seattle area, but most CRM, AI-agent, integration, and web-development work can be handled remotely. Seattle-area businesses are a natural fit because local context helps, but location is not required. Calls, screen shares, and written scopes work well for remote clients.

**What's your minimum project size?**
The project floor is around $5K. Smaller requests can sometimes fit into an hourly retainer if there is an ongoing relationship, but one-off work below that threshold is usually not a fit. This keeps enough room for discovery, implementation, testing, deployment, and handoff.

**How do you bill?**
Fixed-scope projects are billed by milestone with a written scope before work begins. Ongoing work is usually handled through hourly retainers in the $150-$225/hr range depending on scope and support expectations. The billing model is chosen to match the risk: fixed scope for defined builds, hourly for evolving operations.

**Do you build on existing systems or only greenfield?**
Both. Many of the best projects improve an existing workflow by adding a dashboard, automation layer, sync job, or AI triage step without replacing everything. If a system is too brittle to extend safely, OpsHQ Digital will say so and recommend a phased rebuild instead of pretending a patch will solve it.

**Will I own the code?**
Yes, project code and configured assets are handed over according to the written scope. OpsHQ Digital can host, maintain, or monitor systems on retainer, but the client should not be trapped. The exact repo, hosting, credential, and handoff details are documented before delivery.
